quarterly_data.quarter: Canon results briefing Q&A: 2Q 2026 Analyst Meeting Q&A Session Summary (07-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (2Q 2026 analyst meeting Q&A) on semiconductor lithography: the unit sales outlook was raised for memory applications in response to growing demand and lowered for power semiconductor and analog IC applications. Given rising demand from memory customers the company should ideally raise this year's unit sales target further, but after a period of declining orders at the end of last year demand is expanding rapidly and component procurement has not kept pace; the company is asking suppliers to accelerate production schedules. From next year onward it expects production conditions, including at suppliers, to improve and production capacity to increase by more than 20%, allowing production to align more closely with demand.
quarterly_data.figure: lithography production capacity expected to increase by more than 20% from next year

quarterly_data.quarter: Canon results briefing Q&A: 2Q 2026 Analyst Meeting Q&A Session Summary (07-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (2Q 2026 analyst meeting Q&A): for next year the company expects unit sales of both i-line and KrF lithography systems to increase - for i-line, demand for power semiconductor applications is expected to recover; for KrF, demand for memory applications is expected to continue increasing. For the second half of this year it expects sales volume to rise versus a year earlier (last year's volume fell significantly on U.S. price increases), with demand for semiconductor lithography equipment for memory applications expanding and higher Printing unit sales driven by new products.

quarterly_data.quarter: Canon results briefing Q&A: 2Q 2026 Analyst Meeting Q&A Session Summary (07-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (2Q 2026 analyst meeting Q&A) on inventory: under normal circumstances the company targets inventory below 60 days, but it is strategically increasing inventories of semiconductor components, particularly memory-related components that remain in tight supply, and is increasing production capacity in Industrial; it therefore expects inventory turnover days of approximately 65 days at this year-end. Memory prices are generally revised quarterly; the current plan reflects current price levels and assumes some further increase, and while costs could rise further if prices exceed assumptions, the company does not expect significant memory price fluctuations for the rest of the year. Some price increases have already been implemented against higher costs from the Middle East situation and rising memory prices, and additional increases and their timing are being evaluated against the impact on sales volume.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory turnover approximately 65 days expected at year-end (normal target below 60 days)

quarterly_data.quarter: Canon results briefing Q&A: 2Q 2026 Analyst Meeting Q&A Session Summary (07-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (2Q 2026 analyst meeting Q&A): of the total JPY 34.6 billion impact from the Middle East situation, approximately JPY 8.0 billion is lower sales (in the Middle East and in Africa, served through Middle East distribution routes) and the remainder higher costs (production material and component costs tied to higher oil prices, utility and logistics expenses). Second-quarter operating profit fell short of plan, excluding foreign exchange and tariff refunds, due to lower Medical sales from production issues and higher raw material costs mainly in Printing from the Middle East situation; otherwise performance was generally in line with plan. Assuming the Middle East impact continues through the end of September, second-half sales and profit are expected to be more weighted toward the fourth quarter than in a typical year.
quarterly_data.figure: Middle East impact JPY 34.6 billion in total, of which approximately JPY 8.0 billion lower sales

quarterly_data.quarter: Canon results briefing Q&A: 2Q 2026 Analyst Meeting Q&A Session Summary (07-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (2Q 2026 analyst meeting Q&A) on tariffs: the second-quarter positive tariff impact was almost entirely attributable to tariff refunds, as is the full-year outlook (smaller than the second-quarter amount because promotional activities to expand second-half sales are incorporated); more than 90% of the tariff refunds were already received in the first half, with only a small amount expected in the second half; approximately two-thirds of the impact relates to Printing and the remainder to Imaging. In Printing, sales negotiations for printing equipment have become more active in the United States, possibly partly related to tariff refunds received by companies.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 90% of tariff refunds received in H1; approximately two-thirds Printing, remainder Imaging

quarterly_data.quarter: Canon results briefing Q&A: 2Q 2026 Analyst Meeting Q&A Session Summary (07-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (2Q 2026 analyst meeting Q&A) on Medical production issues: problems from the production system transition and a disruption at a supplier prevented on-schedule procurement of components, significantly delaying product deliveries to customers; the company is negotiating individually with suppliers for earlier deliveries and plans to largely normalize production by September. It expects a negative sales impact of approximately JPY 15.0 billion in the second quarter and approximately JPY 25.0 billion in the second half, and a negative profit impact of approximately JPY 20.0 billion for the full year.
quarterly_data.figure: Medical sales impact approximately -JPY 15.0 billion (Q2) and approximately -JPY 25.0 billion (H2); full-year profit impact approximately -JPY 20.0 billion
